person: Walt Brenner, 66, owns a 24-person field-services firm (surveying and renovation crews) with workers in Texas, California and Washington. He does his own HR with a part-time bookkeeper and prints anything longer than a page. Ten unemployment notices have piled up in a stack on his desk, one of them came only by mail, and his Texas field lead insists a laid-off man quit. He is not a computer person and wants to know what each letter wants and what ignoring it costs.
stated_up_front: I've got a pile of unemployment letters from Texas, California and Washington and I don't know which ones have to be answered today. Tell me what each one wants and what it costs me if I let it go, and don't do anything that goes out under my name without asking me first.

facts.about: Today's date for the chore and how many notices are open
facts.truth: 9 October 2026; ten notices open across Texas, California and Washington.

facts.about: The California letter that came only by post
facts.truth: Part-time claim, dated 29 September 2026; his office manager scanned it and he believes it is due today, 9 October.
Laid off for lack of work; the layoff letter is in the personnel file. His field lead, Dale Pruitt, keeps saying Rafael quit.
Let go, but Walt has no written warning and no signed policy for her on file.
Walt's bookkeeper already answered this notice on 2 October.
Walt has never heard of him and finds no record of him on the payroll.
Still on the payroll, working a regular schedule, yet a claim came in her name.
Emailed offer to contest every notice for $95 each; Walt distrusts it after the payroll add-on that charged monthly.

facts.about: Where he finds the company ID when asked
facts.truth: The employer ID number is printed on his payroll stub, near the top.
He prints anything longer than a page and wants large text and no new account.

unknowns: Whether Kofi Mensah's Texas notice is already past its due date, since he only knows the day it arrived
What the Washington due date printed on each request is
How many days California gives him to answer from the date on its notice
Whether a pattern of late or missing answers could cost him relief from charges on his account
